title: Irregular preterite
subtitle: When the past changes its stem
objectives: Distinguish ir and ser through context.
Clarify a sequence when an event is unexpected.
warmup: Retrieve two sentences and one repair strategy from c2-u06. Change the subject or situation in each sentence and explain what changed. Then read today’s objectives and predict where your existing language may be insufficient.

lectures.title: Strong preterite stems
lectures.body: Common irregular stems include tuv-, estuv-, pud-, pus-, sup-, quis-, vin-, hic- and dij-. Most use e, iste, o, imos, isteis, ieron without the regular singular accents: tuve, tuvo, tuvimos. Hacer has hizo in the third singular, preserving pronunciation. J stems use eron in the third plural: dijeron, trajeron, not dijieron. These forms must be learned with examples, not produced by applying a present stem change. Tener → tuve is not tiení. Group verbs by useful events: tuve un problema, pude entrar, puse la dirección, vino una amiga.

lectures.title: Meaning still comes from context
lectures.body: Ir and ser share fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. Fuimos al museo indicates going; fue una experiencia interesante identifies the experience. Dar and ver are short irregulars: di, diste, dio; vi, viste, vio. They do not take the imagined accents dió or vió. Some verbs express a change or bounded achievement in preterite contexts: supe la noticia can mean I found out; pude entrar can mean I managed to enter. These are contextual readings, not a claim that each tense translates to one fixed English verb. Explain the event and result so the intended meaning is clear.

lectures.title: Add the third-person changes that strong stems do not cover
lectures.body:
Not every irregular preterite uses a strong stem such as **tuv-**. Some **-ir** verbs change the stem vowel only in third-person forms: **pedí, pediste, pidió, pedimos, pedisteis, pidieron**; **dormí, dormiste, durmió, dormimos, dormisteis, durmieron**. Compare **Pidieron ayuda** with **Pedimos ayuda**. These are not the full present-tense stem-change patterns carried into the past.

Some verbs also change **i** to **y** between vowels in third-person preterites: **leyó, leyeron**, alongside **leí, leíste, leímos**. Learn **leyó el aviso** as a phrase and compare it with **leí el aviso**. Keep an irregular reference available during homework; independent assessment is a later check of what you can retrieve without it.

Meaning deserves equal attention. **Quise hablar con ella** presents a bounded desire or attempt in context; **no quise** often means refusing. It is too crude to replace every occurrence of querer with “try” solely because it is preterite. Ask what happened before and afterward, then choose a translation that fits the actual event.

reading: El sábado fuimos al museo, pero tuvimos un problema en la entrada. Andrés puso una fecha incorrecta en la reserva. La empleada vio el mensaje y dijo: «Podemos cambiarla». Nos dio dos entradas nuevas. Al final pudimos entrar. La visita fue interesante: vimos una exposición sobre el barrio y supimos por qué cambió su nombre. Lucía hizo varias preguntas. Al salir, Andrés dijo: «La próxima vez voy a revisar la fecha dos veces». Distingue los usos de fuimos y fue; luego identifica el problema, la ayuda y el resultado.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: We had a problem.
quiz.explanation: “Tuvimos un problema” expresses “We had a problem”. “Puso la dirección” instead means “She or he put the address”. “Estuve allí” instead means “I was there during that episode”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: She or he asked a question.
quiz.explanation: “Hizo una pregunta” expresses “She or he asked a question”. “Nos trajeron agua” instead means “They brought us water”. “Vino una amiga” instead means “A friend came”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: They told the truth.
quiz.explanation: “Dijeron la verdad” expresses “They told the truth”. “Vi el mensaje” instead means “I saw the message”. “Al final lo resolvimos” instead means “In the end we solved it”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: I found out the news.
quiz.explanation: “Supe la noticia” expresses “I found out the news”. “Quise ayudar” instead means “I wanted or attempted to help in that episode”. “Tuvimos un problema” instead means “We had a problem”.

quiz.prompt: Choose the expression that communicates this meaning: She or he gave me a ticket.
quiz.explanation: “Me dio una entrada” expresses “She or he gave me a ticket”. “Hizo una pregunta” instead means “She or he asked a question”. “Estuve allí” instead means “I was there during that episode”.

quiz.prompt: Match each English meaning to its Spanish expression. Use each expression once.
answers: ["Me dio una entrada","Fue interesante","Puso la dirección"]
quiz.explanation: “Me dio una entrada” means “She or he gave me a ticket”. “Fue interesante” means “It was interesting”. “Puso la dirección” means “She or he put the address”. Each alternative belongs to a different meaning; check the whole phrase, including its grammatical person and register.

homework.prompt: Read the original text for this unit. Identify its situation, central message, and three supporting details. Then write a new version of 100–140 words for a different person or audience. Use the target patterns, change at least three facts, and explain two revisions.
homework.model:
El sábado fuimos al museo, pero tuvimos un problema en la entrada. Andrés puso una fecha incorrecta en la reserva. La empleada vio el mensaje y dijo: «Podemos cambiarla». Nos dio dos entradas nuevas. Al final pudimos entrar. La visita fue interesante: vimos una exposición sobre el barrio y supimos por qué cambió su nombre. Lucía hizo varias preguntas. Al salir, Andrés dijo: «La próxima vez voy a revisar la fecha dos veces». Distingue los usos de fuimos y fue; luego identifica el problema, la ayuda y el resultado.

This is the source model, not a text to submit unchanged. A successful adaptation retains the communicative purpose while changing relevant forms and facts. Compare with the worked examples for the reasons behind form choices.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: fulfills the specified purpose; organized and comprehensible; target forms support meaning; revisions are explained with examples. 0 = no evidence, 1 = substantial help needed, 2 = effective with some support, 3 = independently effective for this task. Record who evaluated the work.

homework.prompt: Complete the resource assignment, or ask a willing reader to read the original text without showing it to you. First listen for the situation and purpose; listen again for three details and one contrast. Write a 60–100-word listening log naming the source, words actually heard, one uncertainty, and how you checked it. If using local synthesized speech, label it synthetic. Text-only preparation is not completed listening.
homework.model: A useful log separates the speaker’s message from your interpretation: “I heard [specific phrase]; I understood [claim]; I was uncertain about [word/relationship]; checking [text or partner] changed my interpretation to [correction].” Use the unit reading as an answer reference for a read-aloud version, never as evidence of an external speaker’s words.
homework.rubric: 0–2 each: identifies source and listening conditions; retrieves central meaning; supports three details; checks a specific uncertainty. Do not count a copied transcript as independent comprehension.

homework.prompt: Recount a reservation problem to a partner playing a helpful employee. Explain the sequence and result; the partner asks which date or person you mean.
homework.model: Use the original reading/dialogue and the sentence-pattern cards as preparation. Make a brief outline, then put it away. Your partner should introduce a detail you did not prepare. Respond, request clarification if needed, and summarize what you agreed or still disagree about. Solo fallback: record two possible viewpoints and improvise a response after a pause; label it rehearsal.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: task fulfillment, comprehensibility, control of target language, responsiveness to another speaker. A partner or instructor should cite one example per score. Solo rehearsal provides no evidence for live responsiveness; mark that dimension not observed.

homework.prompt: On a later day, retrieve six cards without looking. Use three in a fresh response to the practical task. Identify one recurring form error and one communication difficulty. Produce a corrected example, explain the reason, and schedule a specific follow-up exchange or listening session.
homework.model: Compare your response with these two models: Tuvimos un problema / Hizo una pregunta. A useful reflection explains the function, not just the spelling. Revisit the first worked item and create a different example of its principle.
homework.rubric: Report recall count separately from performance. Reflection is complete when it contains an observed difficulty, an explained correction, a fresh example, and an actionable next session.

task: Recount a reservation problem to a partner playing a helpful employee. Explain the sequence and result; the partner asks which date or person you mean.
culture: Service encounters vary in register and procedure. A polite explanation of a mistake is more useful than assuming a worker can bend a rule. Describe what happened, ask what is possible, and listen to the answer.
selfAssessment: I can use frequent irregular preterite stems.
I can distinguish ir and ser through context.
I can clarify a sequence when an event is unexpected.
remediation: Sort mistakes by form, meaning, and interaction. For form errors, explain a worked example and create a contrasting pair. For comprehension errors, replay a short segment or use a willing reader and verify your interpretation. For interaction difficulties, repeat the practical task with one new constraint. Compare evidence across days; repeated selection of a known answer alone is not mastery.
